Repository Equicom-Crypto/backoffice-core. PR 534 https://github.com/Equicom-Crypto/backoffice-core/pull/534, branch fix/notification-content-freeze into native-v1.
Head e6e2d7d10dcdfd44a358ff2109d680494837ce02; tree b541a19b984510e67f04ad1b717f26cd6a990ea0; base e7037bacad48a10d42db56293e192191d51a0426.
Previous reviewed head baeae8206b3a14731e45485fd4c3c969333010f0. Fix before clean rebase was committed as 8e46eb95. Rebase clean onto e7037bac: original application patch unchanged, original PostgreSQL patch changed import context only. Final added commit e6e2d7d1 gates recipients on frozen category.
PR size 18 files, 1288 additions, 91 deletions, 1379 changed lines, below approximate 1500 split gate. One PR because storage, eligibility and replay must use the same immutable content. Correction changes README, processing.py and content PostgreSQL tests only. No numbered migration or DDL changes. Table already exists. No environment/config/live writes or changes in another repository required. message_key/message_params deferred to 3084 per scope note.

Problem: first PutItem may fail after content is committed. A retry of the same command_id/notification_id may carry a changed category. Incoming TRADING used to drop a frozen SECURITY notification for SUSPENDED users; incoming SECURITY bypassed the status requirement for frozen TRADING. Both ingress and unstored park replay were affected. Competing freeze can also choose a category after the initial absence read.
Fix: centralize new-recipient eligibility in _process_notification_account. Read status with prepared frozen category. If initial inactive or missing candidate has no loaded frozen row, reread existing row without inserting and adopt a concurrent committed category. Before recipient persistence, the freeze insert-if-absent readback winner replaces prepared fields and eligibility is checked again if category changed. Ordinary inactive recipients without a frozen row still create no content. Frozen content never re-resolves template or deeplink. Stored DynamoDB replay retains its existing stored-category gate. GLOBAL/GROUP continues its contract's no USER-status check.
README documents winning frozen category and lazy inactive skip.

Test shape: one new logical parameterized real-PostgreSQL behavior test, eight cases. Existing eight logical tests and 37 cases remain; total nine logical tests and 45 content cases.
Test test_recipient_status_uses_winning_frozen_category table, all with account SUSPENDED:
| Entry | Frozen source | Winner | Incoming | Expected |
| ingress | failed first PutItem retry | SECURITY | TRADING | stored SECURITY |
| ingress | failed first PutItem retry | TRADING | SECURITY | no recipient |
| unstored park replay | failed first PutItem retry | SECURITY | TRADING | stored SECURITY |
| unstored park replay | failed first PutItem retry | TRADING | SECURITY | no recipient |
| ingress | competing freeze | SECURITY | TRADING | stored SECURITY |
| ingress | competing freeze readback | TRADING | SECURITY | no recipient |
| unstored park replay | competing freeze | SECURITY | TRADING | stored SECURITY |
| unstored park replay | competing freeze readback | TRADING | SECURITY | no recipient |
Each asserts winner row unchanged and no rejection outbox row. Retry cases refuse template access after initial committed freeze. Concurrent cases pause loser after initial absence/template read, let another recipient freeze and fail first PutItem, then resume loser. Existing six lazy controls cover disabled, inactive, missing, empty, rejection and write. Existing status tests cover COMPLIANCE exemption, DELETED, missing status and GLOBAL policy; no duplicate new rows needed for those unchanged branches.
